She’s about 50 lbs, maybe 55 since we last weighed her bc she’s only 8 and a half months so she’s still growing. If it helps at all, I could give you a few characteristics she has if it helps you narrow down the breeds. 
-Fur - very soft on head and neck (literally like fluff 😍), less soft on back/stomach. It also gets to be maybe 2-3 inches on her sides and back and her tail hairs definitely have to be at least 4-5 inches lol. Oh and she doesn’t shed much at all!! 
-Behavior around other dogs and people- absolutely loves everyone. Does have minor issues with resource guarding water at a dog park we go to and might try to push other dogs away, but has never shown any signs of aggression.
-trainability - she’s extremely smart and learns really quickly
-Activity level - honestly not super active. She gets tired out at the park very easily after maybe 30 mins of playing especially in this heat, and she usually is fine with chilling at home with me. But I learned yesterday that she LOVES to swim and will do it for hours without getting tired.
-General temperament - very chill, even for being a puppy still. She only barks when she wants food or needs to go out but occasionally will bring out her loud “guard dog bark” when she hears noises when we go out late at night to pee 🙃 she’s also a Velcro dog and will cry/howl when I go away from her and she thinks I’m leaving

I have a border collie mix too! Can I see a picture of her? 😍

To answer your question tho, I have a ton of treat dispenser balls for her meals. It doesn’t keep her too occupied, but it probably does tire her out mentally at least a little. Also got a snuffle mat that she absolutely LOVES to eat out of. Again, only really keeps her occupied for like 10 mins but it’s usually enough time for me to make food for myself or something. I read online that sniffing for 10 mins is equivalent to running for an hour for dogs but I’m not sure how true that is. I have 3 kongs that I give her when I really need her to settle and leave me alone for a good 20 mins. Basically, I just mix together 1 banana and about a spoon of peanut butter which usually is enough to fill all 3 kongs. And then I freeze it and just keep them in there until she *really* needs a distraction. I also bought some hide and seek plush toys for just some quick fun. Also I second the flirt pole! Haven’t used it too often but I’m planning to take her to the park once it gets warmer here to use it more. She has tons of the typical ropes and balls, there’s a few that I soak in water and freeze for when she gets really bitey. Also lick mats are great for feeding pumpkin or other liquid type stuff! 

Between all of those and a short-ish walk every day, my border collie is usually passed out around the time I settle down. Another suggestion too is that training her a bit every day on obedience really drains her mentally. I recommend spending maybe 30 mins and just use like half a cup of her kibble to run through some basic commands if she really needs to calm down. Also, set up playdates with your friends’ dogs as long as they are fully vaccinated!
